title: Duo acceptance: live workspace to organising
intro: Everything built since the live workspace (Phase E) up to organising sessions and projects. Open Duo on the fixture workspace first: run `scripts/acceptance/open-duo.sh` in the duo-v2 repo. Fixtures live in ~/DuoAcceptance (rebuild with `scripts/acceptance/fixtures.py --reset`).
setup: duo2 commands: use `~/repos/duo-v2/build/Duo.app/Contents/Helpers/duo2` from a normal terminal, or plain duo2 inside a Duo session's terminal.

features.title: Projects come from your folders
features.what: The map shows projects from PROJECT.md files, grouped by their parent folder as topics, with goal, health and next step from the frontmatter.
steps: Look at the All projects map.
features.expect: Topics Growth, Payments, Research; projects onboarding, checkout, refunds, reading with their goals; refunds says At risk · Spec review Oct 8.

features.title: Home is the folder with HOME.md, always running
features.what: Home is marked by HOME.md (DL-52) and starts a session if it has none (DL-54).
steps: Look at the left pane on All projects.
features.expect: ★ home with a running Claude Code terminal in `~/DuoAcceptance/workspace/home`.

features.title: + New session
features.what: Starts a Claude Code session in the project folder with a Duo-minted id, filed in the project's `.duo/sessions.json`.
steps: Open checkout.
Click + New session (left pane) or the + in the console tab strip.
features.expect: A new tab opens with Claude Code running in `~/DuoAcceptance/workspace/payments/checkout`.

features.title: No "need you" count at zero
features.what: The toolbar's need-you count isn't drawn when nothing needs you.
steps: On All projects with nothing waiting, look at the toolbar.
features.expect: Only to review, working and idle counts. The count returns (in orange) when a session needs you.

features.title: Needs you, with Claude's actual question
features.what: When a session asks something, the action column shows the real question and options.
steps: In the Home terminal, type: Use AskUserQuestion to ask me whether to lead the readout with revenue or retention.
Don't answer yet; look at the action column and the toolbar.
features.expect: A card with the verbatim question and options; the toolbar shows 1 need you.

features.title: Ready for review, then seen
features.what: A finished turn shows as ready for review until you look at the session.
steps: Start a session in refunds and ask Claude something short.
While it answers, go to All projects.
Then open the session again.
features.expect: After the answer it shows ready for review (◆) with the reply's first line; opening it clears that.

features.title: Session titles that stay put
features.what: Sessions are named from Claude's own title for the conversation, not Claude's random per-process names.
steps: Open reading and look at the session list.
features.expect: Titles like Reading note 1, not names like reading-3f.

features.title: Every past session listed, older ones folded
features.what: A project lists all past sessions in its folder, not just ones Duo started; beyond five they fold under Older · N. The Resume a session button is gone.
steps: Open reading.
Click Older · 4.
features.expect: Five recent sessions, then Older · 4, which expands to four more. No Resume a session button.

features.title: Sessions with the same name stay separate
features.what: Two sessions both titled Untitled scratch show as two rows and open separately.
steps: Open refunds.
Click each Untitled scratch row.
features.expect: Two rows; each opens its own conversation (first scratch thought vs second).

features.title: Documents open in the right pane
features.what: Clicking a file opens it in the editor, styled like the design's document area, with live preview.
steps: Open checkout; in Files, click `docs/prd.md`.
features.expect: Headings in semibold, **15%** shown bold without stars, the link shows as text, task boxes are checkboxes; the line with the caret shows its raw Markdown.

features.title: Autosave, byte-faithful
features.what: Edits save about a second after you stop; untouched text is never rewritten.
steps: Type a sentence in prd.md.
Open `~/DuoAcceptance/workspace/payments/checkout/docs/prd.md` in another editor.
features.expect: Your sentence is there; nothing else changed.

features.title: Windows line endings kept
features.what: A CRLF file stays CRLF after editing.
steps: Open `docs/windows-notes.md`, add a word, wait a second.
In a terminal: `file ~/DuoAcceptance/workspace/payments/checkout/docs/windows-notes.md`
features.expect: file reports CRLF line terminators.

features.title: Files that can't round-trip open read-only
features.what: Mixed line endings or non-UTF-8 text open read-only instead of being rewritten.
steps: Open `docs/mixed-endings.md` and try to type.
Open `docs/legacy-export.txt`.
features.expect: Neither accepts edits; both files are unchanged on disk. (The read-only notice isn't designed yet: Q-20.)

features.title: Spelling, Writing Tools, dictation
features.what: The editor uses macOS text services.
steps: Type recieve teh in a document.
Select a sentence, right-click: look for Writing Tools.
Edit › Start Dictation… and speak a sentence.
features.expect: Misspellings corrected or underlined; Writing Tools available if Apple Intelligence is on; dictation types into the document.

features.title: Format menu: Bold and Italic
features.what: ⌘B and ⌘I work while the editor has focus.
steps: Double-click a word, press ⌘B; another, ⌘I.
features.expect: **word** and *word* in the file.

features.title: Find in a document (⌘F)
features.what: Find searches the whole document, even text scrolled out of view.
steps: Open `docs/long-backlog.md`.
Press ⌘F, search for a word near the end.
features.expect: The find panel opens and finds matches anywhere in the file. (Its look is a placeholder: Q-20.)

features.title: Outside edits merge in, highlighted
features.what: When Claude or another app changes an open file, the change appears, highlighted until your next edit; your unsaved edits are kept.
steps: With prd.md open, append a line to it from another editor or with `echo "hello" >> …/prd.md`.
Then type somewhere.
features.expect: The line appears highlighted; the highlight goes when you type.

features.title: Overlapping edits never overwrite each other
features.what: If an outside change hits text you're editing, Duo keeps your text and pauses autosave instead of overwriting the other change.
steps: Type in the title line of prd.md and, within a second, change the same line in another editor.
In a Duo terminal: `duo2 doc-status docs/prd.md`
features.expect: Your text stays; the file keeps the other change; doc-status says in conflict. (The banner isn't designed yet: Q-20.)

features.title: Document tabs stay open; Project shows PROJECT.md
features.what: Open documents are tabs; the Project tab opens PROJECT.md; a + makes a new file.
steps: Open two documents.
Click Project, then back to a document tab.
Click + in the right pane's tab strip.
features.expect: Tabs persist; Project shows PROJECT.md; + creates `Untitled.md`, opens it and selects its name in Files for renaming.

features.title: ⌘W closes the focused tab
features.what: ⌘W closes the document when the editor has focus, else the session tab; ⇧⌘W closes the window.
steps: Click into a document, press ⌘W.
Click into a session terminal, press ⌘W.
features.expect: The document tab closes; then the session tab closes (the session stays listed and resumable). The window stays.

features.title: New file, folder, from template
features.what: From File (⌘N, ⇧⌘N), the + or a right-click in Files.
steps: Right-click Files' background: New Markdown File, New Folder, New from Template ▸ meeting-notes.
features.expect: Each appears in Files with its name selected for typing; Return keeps it, Esc cancels the rename. Templates list the project's templates/ then Home's.

features.title: Rename, duplicate, move, trash
features.what: Right-click a file or folder in Files, or a document tab.
steps: Rename a file you made; Duplicate it; Move To… a folder; Move to Trash.
features.expect: Each works; an open tab follows a rename or move; Trash closes it and the file is in the macOS Trash.

features.title: Copy path, relative path, link
features.what: Three copy formats.
steps: Right-click `docs/prd.md`: Copy Path, paste; Copy Relative Path, paste; Copy as Link, paste.
features.expect: /Users/…/`docs/prd.md`; `docs/prd.md`; [prd](`docs/prd.md`).

features.title: Reveal in Finder, Open With
features.what: Hand a file to Finder or another app.
steps: Right-click a file: Reveal in Finder; Open With ▸ another app.
features.expect: Finder selects it; the app opens it.

features.title: Send to Claude
features.what: Puts @path into the console session's prompt without sending it.
steps: With a session open in checkout's console, right-click prd.md › Send to Claude.
features.expect: `@docs/prd.md` appears in the prompt, ready for you to write the request.

features.title: Folders without a project file
features.what: Folders with Claude sessions but no PROJECT.md show on the map, marked.
steps: On All projects, look under Elsewhere.
features.expect: scratch (No project file, 2 past sessions) and side-project (Has CLAUDE.md · no project file).

features.title: Make a Project
features.what: Upgrades a folder to a documented project.
steps: Right-click side-project › Make a Project.
Then Edit › Undo.
features.expect: It becomes a project (under Elsewhere) and opens its new PROJECT.md; Undo puts it back as a folder and moves the PROJECT.md to the Trash.

features.title: Move a session to a project
features.what: Right-click or drag a session onto a project; a sheet says exactly what moves; undoable.
steps: Open scratch, right-click Quick question about refund SLAs › Move to Project › refunds.
Read the sheet, click Move.
Edit › Undo.
features.expect: The sheet names the session and says files stay put; it then appears in refunds; Undo returns it.

features.title: Merge a project or folder (sessions only)
features.what: Right-click › Merge Into, or drag a tile onto another.
steps: Drag the scratch tile onto refunds.
Read the sheet, Merge, then Edit › Undo.
features.expect: The sheet lists both sessions and says scratch's folder and files stay; refunds gains them; Undo restores.

features.title: A moved session relocates when resumed
features.what: After a move, the next resume runs /cd so Claude moves the transcript to the new project's folder.
steps: Move Draft a post about pricing (scratch) to checkout.
Open checkout and click the session.
features.expect: Claude opens the old conversation, then shows Moved to …/payments/checkout.

features.title: Sessions survive Claude's 30-day cleanup
features.what: Duo keeps a copy of every listed session (and its tool outputs) and puts it back on resume.
steps: With Duo open for a minute, quit it.
In the repo: `python3 scripts/acceptance/fixtures.py --purge` (simulates the cleanup).
Open Duo again (open-duo.sh), open refunds, click Refund edge cases (purge test).
features.expect: It's still listed by title and resumes with its conversation.

features.title: Carry on in a new session
features.what: Starts a new session that picks up from an archived one.
steps: In a Duo terminal: `duo2 session carry-on <id of the purge-test session>` (the id is in `~/DuoAcceptance/.planted.json`).
features.expect: A new session starts in refunds, reads the archived transcript and summarises where it left off.

features.title: Archive size in `duo2 doctor`
features.what: No limit, but its size is shown.
steps: `duo2 doctor`
features.expect: A line like Session archive: N sessions, X KB.

features.title: duo2 talks to Duo
features.what: ping, status, projects, needs-you, open, help.
steps: duo2 help, then duo2 status, duo2 projects, duo2 open refunds.
features.expect: Answers match the app; open switches Duo to refunds.

features.title: Search across every project
features.what: By meaning and by words, files and sessions, with the app closed too.
steps: `duo2 search customers charged twice`
`duo2 search ERR_REFUND_409`
`duo2 search --kind session interview`
Quit Duo and run a search again.
features.expect: notes/duplicate-billing.md first; errors.md for the exact code; the interview session; results still come back with Duo closed.

features.title: Legacy Duo detection and removal
features.what: Finds legacy Duo's instructions, disables them with a backup, restores them. The fixture is a fake config, not your real ~/.claude.
steps: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/DuoAcceptance/legacy-claude-config duo2 legacy`
`… duo2 legacy disable --yes`
`… duo2 legacy restore <the backup path it printed>`
features.expect: Lists 4 items; disable removes them (your own hook and text stay); restore puts everything back.

features.title: Keep .duo out of git
features.what: In a git repo, Duo offers once to add .duo/ to `.gitignore`.
steps: After opening Duo on the fixtures, look for the alert about onboarding.
features.expect: Add to `.gitignore` writes .duo/ to onboarding/`.gitignore`; Don't Add writes nothing; either answer is remembered.

features.title: Menus
features.what: File (New Markdown File, New Folder, Save, Close Tab, Close Window), Edit (text items, Find, Spelling), Format, View, Go.
steps: Open each menu; try Go › All Projects and Go › Home.
features.expect: Items are present and work; disabled ones are greyed when they don't apply.

features.title: `/clear` keeps the tab with the session
features.what: After `/clear` in a terminal, the tab follows the new conversation.
steps: In a session, type `/clear`, then a short prompt.
features.expect: The tab is renamed after the new conversation; the old session is still listed.
